newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Speculation on Indonesia's rupiah band continues.
newsitem.headline: Speculation on Indonesia's rupiah band continues.

text.p: Speculation on another widening of the Indonesian central bank's dollar-rupiah intervention band lifted the rupiah against the dollar in volatile Friday trading, currency dealers said.
They said many operators shrugged off the speculation but offshore fund managers kept unloading dollars which led some players to believe a widening was imminent.
Central Bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono was close-mouthed on the issue when he met reporters and bankers this week.
"Our monetary policy is eclectic and pragmatic. We keep adjusting whenever it is necessary. But I can't say when it's necessary," he said on Wednesday.
"Our policy is flexible. I can't take the mystery out from the market," he added.
"The rupiah exchange rate will be maintained at a realistic level without anti-export bias," Djiwandono told bankers at an annual bankers' dinner hosted by the central bank on Wednesday.
A state bank economist said the governor's explicit comments were sufficient to indicate an imminent widening was unlikely.
"A band widening now would strengthen the rupiah further which is then violating the export policy," the economist said.

Market analysts said, however, that "creative currency players" had spread rumours. Market talk had ranged from a band widening on Friday afternoon, to imminent action because the bank was holding a meeting, and a news conference had been called.
The central bank denied any meeting was in progress or that a news conference was planned.
The rupiah, meanwhile, continued to appreciate.
It surged to a high of 2,359.0 to the dollar at midday, four points outside of the Bank Indonesia's intervention band of 2,363/2,555 set on Friday.

The central bank intervenes in the foreign exchange market to stabilise the rupiah if the dollar-rupiah rate moves outside of the intervention band, which is set by the bank on a daily basis. Many currency dealers in Jakarta said they did not believe the central bank would bow to market pressure.

Dealers also noted that shrinking interest rate differentials between the dollar and the rupiah, due to declining Indonesian inflation, suggested the potential for a narrowing of the intervention band.
The central bank had also said short-term capital inflows of less than one year, accounted for only five percent of the total capital inflow of $10.5 billion in 1996.
Dealers said rumours of a band widening had been in the market since October after currency dealers were caught by surprise by the central bank's unexpected move in September.
Bank Indonesia widened the band to eight percent from five percent on September 11, after widening it to five percent from three percent on June 13.
Since then, dealers have consistently speculated on another widening because of sustained capital inflows, due to interest rate differentials between the dollar and the rupiah.
